entries.body:
# Death Shot

## Overview
Every hunt has a final moment—the instant when the hunter knows the prey can no longer escape. Death Shot embodies that moment. Rather than relying on overwhelming force, the Ranger waits patiently until their quarry is exhausted, wounded, and vulnerable before loosing a single arrow infused with primal magic to deliver the final blow.

The technique demands exceptional discipline. A Death Shot fired too early wastes its power, while one fired at the perfect moment becomes the inevitable conclusion of the hunt. Among the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are taught that this ability is never used to begin a battle, only to end one.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Every hunt has a final moment—the instant when the hunter knows the prey can no longer escape. Death Shot embodies that moment. Rather than relying on overwhelming force, the Ranger waits patiently until their quarry is exhausted, wounded, and vulnerable before loosing a single arrow infused with primal magic to deliver the final blow.

The technique demands exceptional discipline. A Death Shot fired too early wastes its power, while one fired at the perfect moment becomes the inevitable conclusion of the hunt. Among the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are taught that this ability is never used to begin a battle, only to end one.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 250 MP.
- **Uses:** 1 use per **Long Rest**.
- Make a single ranged weapon attack against a creature within your weapon's range.
- This attack must hit normally.
- Death Shot may only be used against a creature currently affected by your **Hunter's Mark**.
- If the target has **10% or less of its maximum HP** remaining when the attack hits, it is **immediately reduced to 0 HP**.
- If the target has more than **10% of its maximum HP**, Death Shot deals normal weapon damage plus **6d8 Magical Piercing Damage** instead.
- Legendary creatures, Raid Bosses, and creatures specifically designated by the GM as immune to execution effects are instead reduced to **1 HP** if they would be slain by Death Shot.

#### Limitations

- Death Shot cannot critically hit.
- Death Shot may only be used with bows, crossbows, or other ranged weapons approved by the GM.
- The execution effect only applies if the attack successfully hits.

---

### Lore

Death Shot is considered the ultimate expression of a Ranger's patience. It is not a display of strength, but of judgement. The greatest hunters know that every creature has a moment of weakness, and only those with the discipline to wait for that instant are worthy of learning this technique.

Many legendary Huntmasters became famous not for the number of arrows they loosed, but because every Death Shot marked the end of a hunt that others believed impossible. Their arrows became symbols of certainty—the final chapter in every pursuit.

---

> *"The first arrow begins the hunt. The last arrow writes its ending."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Apex Predator**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's understanding of the perfect killing shot deepens, allowing them to recognise the exact instant a wounded quarry can no longer survive. Every heartbeat, every stagger, and every desperate movement reveals an opportunity invisible to ordinary hunters. Death Shot is no longer simply an execution—it is the inevitable conclusion of a hunt carried out with absolute precision.

Veteran Rangers know that the greatest hunters do not waste arrows. They wait patiently, allowing exhaustion, injury, and fear to weaken their quarry before releasing a single arrow that ends the battle. Among the Ranger Lodges, mastering the second rank of Death Shot is considered proof that a Ranger has learned patience above aggression.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 275 MP.
- **Uses:** 1 use per **Long Rest**.
- Make a single ranged weapon attack against a creature within your weapon's range.
- This attack must hit normally.
- The target must be affected by your **Hunter's Mark**.
- If the target has **15% or less of its maximum HP** remaining when the attack hits, it is immediately reduced to **0 HP**.
- If the target has more than **15%** of its maximum HP remaining, Death Shot instead deals normal weapon damage plus **8d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- Legendary creatures, Raid Bosses, and creatures designated by the GM as immune to execution effects are instead reduced to **1 HP** if they would be slain by Death Shot.

#### Limitations

- Death Shot cannot critically hit.
- Death Shot may only be used with bows, crossbows, or other GM-approved ranged weapons.
- The execution effect only occurs if the attack successfully hits.

---

### Lore

To outsiders, Death Shot appears almost supernatural. Experienced Rangers seem capable of predicting the exact instant a creature's strength finally begins to fail, striking with unwavering confidence while others still believe the battle has only just begun.

Within the Ranger Lodges, students are reminded that this technique is earned through discipline rather than talent. Every failed hunt teaches patience, and every successful hunt reinforces a single lesson: the perfect shot is never the first arrow—it is the last.

---

> *"Anyone can loose an arrow. Few possess the patience to know when only one is needed."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger has mastered the art of recognising a quarry's final moments. Every wound, every slowing movement, and every desperate attempt to escape reveals the precise instant when the hunt can be brought to its inevitable conclusion. Death Shot has become more than a finishing technique—it is the embodiment of absolute patience and flawless judgement.

When this technique is unleashed, the Ranger places complete trust in years of experience rather than chance. The arrow is infused with primal magic before being released with unwavering precision, seeking the perfect path to end the hunt. To seasoned Rangers, every creature has a final weakness; only the greatest possess the discipline to wait for it.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 300 MP.
- **Uses:** 1 use per **Long Rest**.
- Make a single ranged weapon attack against a creature within your weapon's range.
- This attack must hit normally.
- The target must be affected by your **Hunter's Mark**.
- If the target has **20% or less of its maximum HP** remaining when the attack hits, it is immediately reduced to **0 HP**.
- If the target has more than **20%** of its maximum HP remaining, Death Shot instead deals normal weapon damage plus **10d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- Legendary creatures, Raid Bosses, and creatures designated by the GM as immune to execution effects are instead reduced to **1 HP** if they would be slain by Death Shot.

#### Limitations

- Death Shot cannot critically hit.
- Death Shot may only be used with bows, crossbows, or other GM-approved ranged weapons.
- The execution effect only occurs if the attack successfully hits.

---

### Lore

Only the most disciplined Rangers ever reach the third rank of Death Shot. They no longer see a wounded enemy—they see the inevitable conclusion of the hunt. Every lesson learned through countless battles allows them to recognise the exact moment when resistance has ended, even if the quarry has yet to realise it.

Within the Ranger Lodges, this mastery is regarded with immense respect. Rangers capable of performing Death Shot are often entrusted with eliminating the most dangerous beasts and monsters in Asteria, where hesitation could mean the difference between victory and extinction.

---

> *"Mercy belongs to the hunter who ends the suffering with a single arrow."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's mastery over Death Shot has become legendary. Their understanding of anatomy, instinct, and timing has reached a point where they can identify a quarry's final weakness with only a glance. Every heartbeat, every faltering step, and every sign of fatigue reveals the perfect opportunity to deliver the finishing blow.

The arrow itself becomes a vessel of primal magic, carrying the Ranger's unwavering intent. Once released, it represents the culmination of an entire hunt, guided by years of discipline rather than emotion. To face a Ranger capable of this technique is to know that every mistake brings the inevitable end one step closer.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 325 MP.
- **Uses:** 1 use per **Long Rest**.
- Make a single ranged weapon attack against a creature within your weapon's range.
- This attack must hit normally.
- The target must be affected by your **Hunter's Mark**.
- If the target has **25% or less of its maximum HP** remaining when the attack hits, it is immediately reduced to **0 HP**.
- If the target has more than **25%** of its maximum HP remaining, Death Shot instead deals normal weapon damage plus **12d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- Legendary creatures, Raid Bosses, and creatures designated by the GM as immune to execution effects are instead reduced to **1 HP** if they would be slain by Death Shot.
- If Death Shot successfully reduces a creature to **0 HP**, you immediately regain **100 MP** and may immediately transfer **Hunter's Mark** to another creature within your weapon's range without paying its Mana Cost.

#### Limitations

- Death Shot cannot critically hit.
- Death Shot may only be used with bows, crossbows, or other GM-approved ranged weapons.
- The execution effect only occurs if the attack successfully hits.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, the fourth rank of Death Shot is regarded as the mark of a true Huntmaster. Those who achieve it are no longer simply skilled archers—they are executioners of the wild, capable of ending even the fiercest hunts with a single perfectly placed arrow.

Many of Asteria's greatest monsters met their end beneath this technique. The stories speak not of prolonged battles, but of one final arrow released at precisely the right moment. To those who witnessed it, the hunt did not end with violence—it ended with certainty.

---

> *"Every hunt ends with a final breath. My arrow simply decides when that breath is taken."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

Death Shot has become the ultimate expression of the Ranger's purpose. The hunt has reached its inevitable conclusion, and the Ranger requires only a single arrow to deliver judgement. Every lesson learned throughout a lifetime of tracking, observing, and overcoming the world's deadliest creatures culminates in this one technique.

As the arrow is infused with immense primal magic, the Ranger waits with unwavering patience for the exact instant their quarry falters. There is no hesitation, no wasted movement, and no uncertainty. When the arrow is finally released, it carries the certainty that every hunt must eventually end.

Among the Ranger Lodges, mastering the fifth rank of Death Shot is considered the highest honour a hunter can achieve. It is said that once an Apex Predator has chosen the final moment, even the greatest monsters cannot escape their fate.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 350 MP.
- **Uses:** 1 use per **Long Rest**.
- Make a single ranged weapon attack against a creature within your weapon's range.
- This attack must hit normally.
- The target must be affected by your **Hunter's Mark**.
- If the target has **30% or less of its maximum HP** remaining when the attack hits, it is immediately reduced to **0 HP**.
- If the target has more than **30%** of its maximum HP remaining, Death Shot instead deals normal weapon damage plus **15d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- Legendary creatures, Raid Bosses, Mythic creatures, and creatures designated by the GM as immune to execution effects are instead reduced to **1 HP** if they would be slain by Death Shot.
- If Death Shot reduces a creature to **0 HP**:
  - Immediately regain **150 MP**.
  - You may immediately transfer **Hunter's Mark** to another creature within your weapon's range without paying its Mana Cost.
  - You may immediately make **one standard ranged weapon attack** against the newly marked creature. This attack does **not** benefit from Death Shot.

#### Limitations

- Death Shot cannot critically hit.
- Death Shot may only be used with bows, crossbows, or other GM-approved ranged weapons.
- The execution effect only occurs if the attack successfully hits.
- The bonus ranged attack may only occur once per use of Death Shot.

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Rangers throughout Asteria's history have ever mastered the fifth rank of Death Shot. Their names have become legend not because they hunted the greatest beasts, but because they never failed to finish a hunt once they committed to it. Dragons, eldritch horrors, ancient predators, and creatures thought impossible to slay all eventually fell to a single perfectly timed arrow.

Within the Ranger Lodges, Death Shot is regarded as the final lesson every hunter strives toward. It is not a display of overwhelming strength, but the ultimate reward for patience, discipline, and absolute mastery of the hunt. To wield Death Shot is to understand that every creature, no matter how mighty, has a final moment—and a true Ranger will always recognise it.

---

> *"Every hunt begins with hope. Every hunt ends with one perfect arrow."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Apex Predator**

entries.body:
# Arcane Echo

## Overview
A Spellblade's mastery extends beyond blades and spells. Through careful manipulation of arcane energy, they learn to leave behind fragments of their presence, creating convincing images that linger within the world.

These manifestations, known as Arcane Echoes, are not living beings, summoned creatures, or independent entities. They are reflections of the Spellblade's arcane signature given temporary form. To an observer, the Echo appears identical to its creator, standing motionless as though waiting for the perfect moment to act.

At Rank 1, the Echo lacks intelligence, movement, and substance. It cannot attack, speak, cast spells, or interact with the world. Its purpose is deception. Whether used to distract enemies, conceal the Spellblade's true position, or create uncertainty during an encounter, the Echo forces opponents to question what they are seeing.

Many Spellblades consider Arcane Echo one of the most valuable tactical abilities available to them. A well-placed illusion can create opportunities that brute force never could.

## Rank 1
### Description

A Spellblade's mastery extends beyond blades and spells. Through careful manipulation of arcane energy, they learn to leave behind fragments of their presence, creating convincing images that linger within the world.

These manifestations, known as Arcane Echoes, are not living beings, summoned creatures, or independent entities. They are reflections of the Spellblade's arcane signature given temporary form. To an observer, the Echo appears identical to its creator, standing motionless as though waiting for the perfect moment to act.

At Rank 1, the Echo lacks intelligence, movement, and substance. It cannot attack, speak, cast spells, or interact with the world. Its purpose is deception. Whether used to distract enemies, conceal the Spellblade's true position, or create uncertainty during an encounter, the Echo forces opponents to question what they are seeing.

Many Spellblades consider Arcane Echo one of the most valuable tactical abilities available to them. A well-placed illusion can create opportunities that brute force never could.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to create an Arcane Echo.
- The Echo appears within **5 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echo remains for **1 minute** or until destroyed.
- Only **one Arcane Echo** may exist at a time.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

The Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Remains completely stationary.
- Cannot move.
- Cannot attack.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot speak.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects the Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must bet a DC10

On a success:
- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:
- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

#### Destruction

The Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of one Echo active at a time.
- The Echo cannot move.
- The Echo cannot perform actions.
- The Echo cannot activate abilities.
- The Echo provides no direct offensive benefits.
- The Echo is clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

Among the oldest Spellblade traditions, Arcane Echo was originally developed as a dueling technique. Practitioners sought methods of confusing opponents without relying on brute force or overwhelming magical power.

The first Echoes were crude and unstable, often flickering in and out of existence. Over generations, Spellblades refined the technique until their illusions became nearly indistinguishable from the real practitioner at a glance.

Many instructors teach that Arcane Echo embodies an important lesson: victory does not always belong to the strongest combatant. Sometimes it belongs to the one who controls what their opponent believes.

Veteran Spellblades often claim that the greatest strength of an Echo is not convincing an enemy that it is real. It is making them doubt whether anything they see can be trusted.

> "A sword threatens the body. Uncertainty threatens the mind."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hall

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Spellblade's understanding of illusion and arcane projection improves, their Arcane Echo becomes more stable and convincing. The image no longer flickers as easily, allowing it to remain present for extended periods and over greater distances.

The Echo remains incapable of movement or independent action, but the quality of the illusion improves considerably. Fine details such as armour, clothing, weapons, and posture are replicated with greater accuracy, making it more difficult for observers to immediately identify the deception.

Experienced Spellblades often use Arcane Echo as a scouting aid, distraction, or means of controlling the battlefield. An enemy forced to question what they are seeing is already at a disadvantage.

While still a simple projection, the Echo begins to feel less like a magical construct and more like a genuine reflection of the Spellblade's presence.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to create an Arcane Echo.
- The Echo appears within **10 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echo remains for **5 minutes** or until destroyed.
- Only **one Arcane Echo** may exist at a time.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

The Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Remains completely stationary.
- Cannot move.
- Cannot attack.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot speak.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Improved Illusion

The Arcane Echo now reproduces:

- Current equipment.
- Current weapon.
- Current armour.
- Current stance and posture.

Observers see the Echo exactly as the Spellblade appeared when the Echo was created.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects the Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must beat a **DC 12**.

On a success:

- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:

- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

#### Destruction

The Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of one Echo active at a time.
- The Echo cannot move.
- The Echo cannot perform actions.
- The Echo cannot activate abilities.
- The Echo provides no direct offensive benefits.
- The Echo is clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

Among Spellblade academies, Rank II is often referred to as the Stage of Refinement. At this point, the Echo becomes convincing enough that even experienced combatants may hesitate before dismissing it as a simple illusion.

The greatest strength of Arcane Echo has never been the illusion itself. It is the uncertainty it creates. A moment of hesitation can be worth more than any blade strike, and many Spellblades have secured victory through deception rather than force.

Records from the Mirror Hall tell of duelists who won entire tournaments without ever striking first, relying instead on confusion, misdirection, and flawless positioning. Their Echoes forced opponents to second-guess every decision they made.

A wise Spellblade understands that battles are fought in both the mind and the body. Arcane Echo targets the former long before the latter.

> "When your enemy doubts their own eyes, the battle is already half won."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hall

## Rank 3
### Description

The Spellblade's Arcane Echo evolves beyond a simple stationary illusion. Through greater control over mana and projection, the Echo can now imitate basic movement, making it significantly more difficult to distinguish from the real Spellblade at a glance.

The movement is limited and lacks true intelligence. The Echo cannot make decisions, engage in combat, or interact with the world around it. Instead, it follows simple commands issued by its creator, moving in a deliberate and predictable manner.

For the first time, the Arcane Echo begins to create genuine uncertainty on the battlefield. Enemies can no longer rely on the Echo remaining where it was created, forcing them to spend precious moments determining which Spellblade is real.

Many veteran Spellblades consider this the point where Arcane Echo becomes a true battlefield deception technique rather than a simple distraction.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to create an Arcane Echo.
- The Echo appears within **15 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echo remains for **10 minutes** or until destroyed.
- Only **one Arcane Echo** may exist at a time.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

The Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Can move up to **3 metres per turn**.
- Cannot attack.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot speak.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Controlled Movement

The Spellblade may direct the Echo to:

- Walk.
- Turn.
- Change facing.
- Follow simple movement paths.

The Echo cannot:

- Run.
- Jump.
- Climb.
- Use talents.
- Mimic combat actions.

#### Improved Illusion

The Arcane Echo now reproduces:

- Current equipment.
- Current weapon.
- Current armour.
- Current stance and posture.
- Basic walking movements.

Observers see the Echo exactly as the Spellblade appeared when the Echo was created.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects the Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must beat a **DC 14**.

On a success:

- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:

- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

#### Destruction

The Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of one Echo active at a time.
- The Echo cannot perform actions.
- The Echo cannot activate abilities.
- The Echo cannot attack.
- The Echo provides no direct offensive benefits.
- The Echo is clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade traditions, Rank III is known as the Stage of Motion. It represents the point where an Echo ceases to be a simple image and begins to imitate life itself.

Many apprentices are surprised to learn that movement is often more convincing than appearance. A perfectly crafted illusion that never moves quickly becomes suspicious, while even a simple projection can appear genuine when it behaves naturally.

Historical accounts tell of Spellblades using moving Echoes to lure enemies into traps, distract guards, and create confusion during battles. Entire skirmishes have been decided by opponents chasing a false target while the real Spellblade positioned themselves elsewhere.

Masters of Arcane Echo often remind their students that deception is not about creating a perfect lie. It is about creating enough doubt that the truth becomes difficult to see.

> "The eye sees what it expects to see. A moving shadow is often enough."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hall

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade's mastery of Arcane Echo reaches a level where a single illusion is no longer sufficient. Through refined control over their mana, they learn to divide their arcane signature between multiple projections, creating a web of uncertainty across the battlefield.

Each Echo remains a construct of mana rather than a true duplicate, yet the presence of multiple projections dramatically increases the difficulty of identifying the real Spellblade. Enemies can no longer focus on a single target, forcing them to question every movement and every decision.

The Echoes are still limited in their capabilities, unable to fight or cast spells, but their ability to move independently creates a powerful tool for deception, scouting, distraction, and battlefield manipulation.

Among veteran Spellblades, Rank IV is often considered the point where Arcane Echo becomes genuinely dangerous. Not because the Echoes can harm an opponent, but because they make mistakes far more likely.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to create Arcane Echoes.
- Create up to **2 Arcane Echoes** within **20 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echoes remain for **15 minutes** or until destroyed.
- Both Echoes may exist simultaneously.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

Each Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Can move up to **5 metres per turn**.
- Cannot attack.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot speak.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Independent Movement

The Spellblade may direct each Echo individually.

Each Echo may:

- Walk.
- Turn.
- Change facing.
- Follow simple movement paths.
- Move in different directions from other Echoes.

The Echoes cannot:

- Run.
- Jump.
- Climb.
- Use talents.
- Mimic combat actions.

#### Advanced Illusion

The Echoes now reproduce:

- Current equipment.
- Current weapon.
- Current armour.
- Current stance and posture.
- Basic walking movements.
- Minor idle movements such as shifting weight, looking around, and adjusting stance.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects an Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must beat a **DC 16**.

On a success:

- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:

- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

A creature must investigate each Echo separately.

#### Destruction

An Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of two Echoes active at a time.
- Echoes cannot perform actions.
- Echoes cannot activate abilities.
- Echoes cannot attack.
- Echoes provide no direct offensive benefits.
- Echoes are clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

Rank IV is often referred to as the Stage of Multiplicity within the Mirror Hall traditions. The Spellblade learns that confusion does not come from creating a perfect illusion—it comes from creating too many possibilities.

Military records contain numerous accounts of enemy formations wasting valuable time and resources attempting to identify the true Spellblade among multiple projections. Some commanders even ordered volleys of arrows directed at every visible target, only to discover they had spent precious resources attacking illusions.

Masters of Arcane Echo often teach that deception is strongest when certainty becomes impossible. When an opponent can no longer trust their own eyes, every decision becomes slower, every action becomes hesitant, and every mistake becomes more likely.

To a skilled Spellblade, uncertainty is a weapon as sharp as any blade.

> "One illusion creates doubt. Two create confusion. Beyond that, the enemy defeats themselves."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hall

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Echo reaches its ultimate form, allowing the Spellblade to create projections so convincing that even experienced warriors struggle to distinguish illusion from reality. The Echoes no longer merely stand or move—they imitate the behaviour of their creator with startling accuracy.

Through exceptional control over mana, the Spellblade can command their Echoes to mimic simple combat actions, gestures, and movements. Though still incapable of causing harm, these projections create uncertainty on a scale that few opponents are prepared to face.

Enemies attempting to identify the real Spellblade must now contend with multiple moving targets, each behaving as though it could be genuine. Every hesitation creates an opportunity, and every mistake can shift the outcome of a battle.

Among the ancient Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the Stage of Mirrors. It is said that a master of Arcane Echo never enters a battle alone, for every reflection of their presence becomes another threat their enemies must account for.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to create Arcane Echoes.
- Create up to **3 Arcane Echoes** within **25 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echoes remain for **30 minutes** or until destroyed.
- All three Echoes may exist simultaneously.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

Each Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Can move up to **6 metres per turn**.
- Cannot deal damage.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Advanced Mimicry

The Echoes may perform:

- Walking.
- Running.
- Turning.
- Drawing or sheathing weapons.
- Combat stances.
- Practice swings.
- Defensive postures.
- Pointing and gesturing.

The Echoes cannot:

- Deal damage.
- Cast spells.
- Activate talents.
- Speak.
- Physically interact with creatures or objects.

#### Masterful Illusion

The Echoes now reproduce:

- Current equipment.
- Current weapon.
- Current armour.
- Current stance and posture.
- Movement patterns.
- Combat motions.
- Basic behavioural mannerisms.

To casual observation, the Echoes are nearly indistinguishable from the real Spellblade.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects an Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must beat a **DC 18**.

On a success:

- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:

- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

A creature must investigate each Echo separately.

#### Destruction

An Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of three Echoes active at a time.
- Echoes cannot deal damage.
- Echoes cannot activate abilities.
- Echoes cannot cast spells.
- Echoes provide no direct offensive benefits.
- Echoes are clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

The greatest masters of Arcane Echo are remembered throughout Asteria as impossible opponents to track. Witnesses often described battles where multiple Spellblades appeared to be fighting at once, each moving with such confidence that identifying the real combatant became nearly impossible.

Legends tell of duelists who defeated stronger opponents through deception alone, exhausting their enemies as they chased illusions while the true Spellblade waited for the perfect opportunity to strike. Whether these stories are exaggerated or entirely truthful remains a matter of debate.

Within the Mirror Hall, Rank V is regarded as the pinnacle of illusionary combat. Students who achieve this level are taught that the purpose of Arcane Echo is not to create falsehoods, but to create uncertainty. When certainty disappears, mistakes follow.

A master Spellblade understands that a blade can wound the body, but doubt can unravel an entire battle.

> "The enemy sees four Spellblades. The wise enemy asks which one is real. The fool attacks the first one they see."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hallv

# Arcane Edge

## Overview
The defining trait of every Spellblade is the ability to merge martial skill with arcane power. Rather than casting magic separately from combat, they learn to channel mana directly through their weapon, temporarily transforming it into a conduit of raw magical energy.

When Arcane Edge is activated, mana flows from the Spellblade's core into the weapon, causing its edge to shimmer with arcane light. Every strike delivered while the enchantment is active carries a pulse of magical force, allowing the Spellblade to inflict wounds that ordinary steel alone could never achieve.

At Rank I, maintaining this enchantment is physically and mentally demanding, limiting how long the weapon can remain empowered. Even so, mastering this technique marks the first true step towards becoming a Spellblade, teaching that the greatest weapon is one where steel and mana strike together as one.

## Rank 1
### Description

The defining trait of every Spellblade is the ability to merge martial skill with arcane power. Rather than casting magic separately from combat, they learn to channel mana directly through their weapon, temporarily transforming it into a conduit of raw magical energy.

When Arcane Edge is activated, mana flows from the Spellblade's core into the weapon, causing its edge to shimmer with arcane light. Every strike delivered while the enchantment is active carries a pulse of magical force, allowing the Spellblade to inflict wounds that ordinary steel alone could never achieve.

At Rank I, maintaining this enchantment is physically and mentally demanding, limiting how long the weapon can remain empowered. Even so, mastering this technique marks the first true step towards becoming a Spellblade, teaching that the greatest weapon is one where steel and mana strike together as one.

### Effects

- Spend **15 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **2 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d4 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Arcane Edge is one of the oldest techniques preserved within the Spellblade Orders. Before learning advanced combat magic, every apprentice is taught that a weapon should become an extension of their mana, not merely a piece of sharpened steel.

The earliest practitioners discovered that even a simple infusion of mana dramatically increased the lethality of a weapon without requiring complex enchantments. Although temporary, this technique proved invaluable in battle, allowing Spellblades to adapt instantly to changing situations without relying upon permanently enchanted arms.

To this day, many masters consider Arcane Edge the moment an apprentice truly earns the title of Spellblade, for it is the first time they successfully unite steel and sorcery into a single weapon.

> *"A blade without mana is only steel. A blade with mana carries the will of its master."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Spellblade's control over mana improves, so too does their ability to sustain an arcane enchantment upon their weapon. Rather than releasing short bursts of unstable energy, the Spellblade learns to maintain a steadier flow of mana, strengthening both the duration and potency of Arcane Edge.

The weapon's aura burns brighter and the magical energy coursing through its edge becomes more refined. Each successful strike releases a greater surge of arcane power, allowing the Spellblade to carve through both physical armour and magical defences with increasing efficiency.

Rank II represents the first significant refinement of Arcane Edge. The enchantment lasts longer, strikes harder, and requires greater discipline to maintain. Veteran Spellblades often encourage apprentices to master this rank before pursuing more advanced offensive techniques, as a stable Arcane Edge forms the foundation of nearly every magical weapon art practiced within the Order.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **3 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d6 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Spellblade historians often refer to Rank II as the stage where mana and steel begin to trust one another. The unstable surges experienced by novices become controlled currents, allowing the weapon to channel greater power without risking the integrity of the blade.

Many ancient duelling schools considered mastery of this rank a rite of passage. Only once a Spellblade could reliably maintain Arcane Edge throughout an entire duel were they permitted to study the more advanced techniques of their Order.

Although stronger enchantments await those who continue their training, Rank II is where Arcane Edge first begins to resemble the legendary weapon enchantment that made the Spellblade Orders famous across Asteria.

> *"Power without control burns the blade. Control allows the blade to burn the world."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

With greater experience, the Spellblade no longer struggles to contain the immense flow of mana coursing through their weapon. Arcane Edge becomes a stable combat enchantment, allowing the Spellblade to maintain overwhelming magical pressure throughout prolonged engagements.

When activated, the weapon radiates a vibrant arcane aura as streams of mana race across its surface. Every strike lands with both physical force and concentrated magical energy, making each blow increasingly difficult to defend against. The weapon itself feels lighter in the Spellblade's hands, as if recognising the mana flowing through it and responding as a natural extension of its wielder.

Rank III is often regarded as the point where Arcane Edge becomes a signature combat technique rather than a simple enhancement. Spellblades capable of maintaining this level of enchantment are recognised as experienced warriors whose mastery of blade and mana has become second nature.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **3 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d8 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Among the Spellblade Orders, Rank III is known as the **Awakened Edge**. It is the stage where apprentices cease relying on conscious effort to maintain the enchantment, allowing mana to flow naturally between themselves and their weapon.

Many renowned Spellblades have described this experience as hearing the blade "sing" for the first time. Whether this is merely poetic tradition or evidence of a deeper bond between mana and steel remains a topic of debate among arcane scholars.

Regardless of the explanation, every master agrees on one truth: once a Spellblade reaches this stage, their weapon is no longer simply carried into battle—it becomes an extension of their own soul.

> *"When your blade begins to answer your mana without hesitation, you no longer wield a weapon—you wield yourself."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade has mastered the art of maintaining an Arcane Edge through even the fiercest battles. Mana now flows effortlessly from their core into their weapon, creating a stable enchantment that burns with immense arcane power. The weapon hums with energy, its edge glowing brightly as each strike releases concentrated bursts of magic.

Unlike earlier ranks, maintaining the enchantment no longer demands complete focus. The Spellblade has learned to weave mana into every movement, allowing them to fight naturally while their weapon remains empowered. Every swing reinforces the harmony between blade and magic, making the Spellblade an increasingly dangerous opponent in prolonged combat.

Rank IV is regarded as the hallmark of veteran Spellblades. The enchantment is no longer an experimental technique but a reliable extension of their combat style, capable of carrying them through the most demanding encounters. Few warriors can withstand a sustained assault from a Spellblade whose Arcane Edge has reached this level of refinement.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **4 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d10 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Veteran's Edge**. Reaching this stage signifies years of disciplined training and countless battles fought with blade and mana working as one.

Many master smiths claim they can recognise a veteran Spellblade simply by examining their weapon. Though Arcane Edge leaves no permanent enchantment behind, repeated infusions gradually leave faint traces of mana within the steel, a testament to the countless times it has served as a conduit for arcane power.

To fellow Spellblades, the sight of a brilliantly glowing blade is both inspiring and intimidating. It is a reminder that true mastery is not measured by the strength of a single strike, but by the ability to maintain perfect harmony between steel and sorcery throughout an entire battle.

> *"A true Spellblade does not borrow power from magic. They teach their blade to breathe it."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Edge reaches its ultimate form, becoming the signature technique of a true Spellblade Master. The flow of mana between wielder and weapon is now effortless, allowing the Spellblade to maintain an enchantment of extraordinary potency without interrupting the rhythm of combat. Every strike becomes a perfect union of martial precision and arcane might.

When activated, the weapon blazes with brilliant arcane light, its edge surrounded by streams of concentrated mana that shimmer with every movement. The enchantment resonates through the blade, releasing devastating bursts of magical energy with every successful strike. To those who witness it, the weapon appears less like forged steel and more like a living extension of the Spellblade's soul.

Few warriors ever achieve this level of mastery. Rank V is reserved for those who have devoted years to perfecting the harmony between magic and swordsmanship. Every swing demonstrates absolute control, proving that the greatest strength of a Spellblade is not their magic or their blade alone, but the flawless balance between the two.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **8 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d12 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

The ancient Spellblade Orders refer to this technique as the **Master's Edge**, the highest expression of their martial philosophy. It is said that the greatest Spellblades no longer distinguish between themselves, their mana, and their weapon. All three become one, moving with perfect unity in battle.

Legends tell of masters whose Arcane Edge shone so brightly that it illuminated entire battlefields, their enchanted blades carving through monsters, enchanted armour, and even powerful magical barriers. Whether these tales have grown through centuries of retelling is unknown, but they remain a source of inspiration for every aspiring Spellblade.

To achieve Rank V is to embody everything the Spellblade path represents. It is the culmination of countless hours of discipline, sacrifice, and unwavering dedication to mastering both steel and sorcery. Few will ever wield an Arcane Edge of this calibre, and fewer still will be remembered for doing so.

> *"When steel and mana can no longer be told apart, you have reached the edge where legends are born."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

# Arcane Reflex

## Overview
A Spellblade survives not by enduring every strike, but by avoiding the ones that matter.

Through training and repeated exposure to combat, the Spellblade learns to channel mana through their nervous system, briefly accelerating their reactions beyond normal limits. This surge of arcane energy allows them to read danger more quickly and adjust their position in the instant before an attack lands.

To outside observers, the movement appears insignificant—a slight shift of the shoulder, a subtle turn of the body, or a single step placed at precisely the right moment. Yet those tiny adjustments often mean the difference between a devastating blow and a harmless miss.

At Rank 1, Arcane Reflex represents the beginning of this discipline. The Spellblade learns to instinctively call upon mana when threatened, increasing their ability to evade incoming attacks.

## Rank 1
### Description

A Spellblade survives not by enduring every strike, but by avoiding the ones that matter.

Through training and repeated exposure to combat, the Spellblade learns to channel mana through their nervous system, briefly accelerating their reactions beyond normal limits. This surge of arcane energy allows them to read danger more quickly and adjust their position in the instant before an attack lands.

To outside observers, the movement appears insignificant—a slight shift of the shoulder, a subtle turn of the body, or a single step placed at precisely the right moment. Yet those tiny adjustments often mean the difference between a devastating blow and a harmless miss.

At Rank 1, Arcane Reflex represents the beginning of this discipline. The Spellblade learns to instinctively call upon mana when threatened, increasing their ability to evade incoming attacks.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **12 MP**.
- Gain **+1 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the attack that triggered the reaction.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses an action from you next round.

### Lore

The earliest Spellblade instructors taught that survival begins with awareness. Before a warrior can master advanced techniques, they must first learn to recognise danger and respond to it without hesitation.

Arcane Reflex was developed as a means of enhancing this instinct through mana. Rather than creating barriers or relying on heavy armour, the Spellblade learns to trust their reactions and use magic to sharpen them.

Many apprentices underestimate the value of such a simple technique. Veteran Spellblades rarely make the same mistake. They understand that surviving a battle is often more important than winning a single exchange.

Among the older duelling schools, students are often told that every great Spellblade has one thing in common: they lived long enough to become one.

> "Victory belongs to those who survive long enough to claim it."
>
> — Blademaster Kaelis Vorn, Instructor of the Azure Path

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Spellblade's mastery of Arcane Reflex grows, they learn that avoidance is not always possible. Even the fastest reaction cannot prevent every strike from finding its mark.

Rather than relying solely on evasion, the Spellblade learns to reinforce their body with mana at the moment of impact. Arcane energy instinctively flows to vulnerable areas, lessening the force of incoming blows and reducing the harm suffered when an attack cannot be completely avoided.

This technique requires precise timing. Too early and mana is wasted. Too late and the attack lands with full force. Through constant training, the Spellblade develops the instinct to react at exactly the right moment.

At Rank 2, Arcane Reflex evolves from simple avoidance into a layered defensive technique. The Spellblade becomes harder to hit and more resilient when they are struck.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **15 MP**.
- Gain **+2 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the attack that triggered the reaction.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses an action from you next round.

### Lore

Among veteran Spellblades, Rank 2 is often called the Lesson of Reality. It teaches a simple truth: perfection is impossible.

No matter how skilled a warrior becomes, there will always be attacks that cannot be completely avoided. The difference between a novice and a master is not whether they are hit, but how they respond when they are.

The arcane reinforcement techniques used by Spellblades were originally developed during the Age of Fractured Crowns, when battlefield mages sought ways to survive against heavily armoured opponents. Rather than matching strength with strength, they learned to redirect and disperse force through carefully controlled mana flows.

Modern Spellblades continue this tradition. Every successful use of Arcane Reflex strengthens the connection between instinct and magic, allowing them to survive situations that would cripple lesser combatants.

> "The greatest warriors are not those who never fall. They are those who learn how to fall without breaking."
>
> — High Spellblade Arkanis Thorne, Warden of the Azure Depths

## Rank 3
### Description

A seasoned Spellblade understands that combat is a balance between avoidance and endurance. While Arcane Reflex allows them to evade many attacks, experience teaches that not every strike can be escaped completely.

As their control over mana improves, the Spellblade learns to instinctively direct arcane energy to vulnerable areas of the body at the moment of impact. This reinforcement does not stop an attack, but it can lessen the force behind it and prevent potentially devastating injuries.

The process occurs almost subconsciously. The moment danger is recognised, mana surges through the body, sharpening reflexes while simultaneously preparing for the possibility of failure. If the attack misses, the Spellblade avoids harm entirely. If it lands, the mana absorbs part of the impact.

At Rank 3, Arcane Reflex becomes a complete defensive technique, providing both improved evasion and limited protection when avoidance alone is not enough.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **18 MP**.
- Gain **+3 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the attack that triggered the reaction.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses your Reaction for the round.

### Lore

Among the ancient Spellblade Orders, Rank 3 is known as the Stage of Resilience. It marks the point where a practitioner learns that survival is not determined solely by avoiding danger, but by enduring it when necessary.

The earliest forms of Arcane Mitigation were developed during prolonged border wars where Spellblades often found themselves outnumbered and unable to evade every attack. By learning to reinforce their bodies with mana at the moment of impact, they dramatically improved their chances of surviving extended engagements.

Veteran instructors often describe this stage as a shift in mindset. Students stop viewing defense as a single action and begin understanding it as a layered system. First avoid the attack. If that fails, lessen the damage. If that fails, remain standing.

Many Spellblades consider Rank 3 the moment Arcane Reflex becomes truly reliable, transforming it from a useful trick into a cornerstone of battlefield survival.

> "The perfect defense is not avoiding every blow. It is surviving the ones you cannot."
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aethon Vale, Master of the Sapphire Hall

## Rank 4
### Description

Arcane Reflex evolves beyond simple defense and becomes a tool of battlefield control. The Spellblade no longer focuses solely on avoiding danger or enduring a strike—they learn to use every attack against them as an opportunity to reposition and reclaim the advantage.

Through years of combat experience, the Spellblade's reactions become intertwined with their mana flow. The moment an attack is launched, their body instinctively prepares not only to evade or mitigate the strike, but also to move into a more favorable position.

To observers, the movement appears unnatural. An attack is thrown, a flash of mana erupts around the Spellblade, and suddenly they are somewhere else entirely. What seemed like a successful attack becomes an opening for the Spellblade to exploit.

At Rank 4, Arcane Reflex transforms from a purely defensive talent into a tactical one. Surviving is no longer the goal—controlling the battlefield is.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **21 MP**.
- Gain **+4 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the triggering attack.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses your Reaction for the round.

#### Arcane Mitigation

If the triggering attack still hits:

- Reduce the damage taken by **1d4**. Can not reduce damage to 0.

### Lore

Among veteran Spellblades, Rank 4 is known as the Stage of Control. At this point, practitioners stop reacting to the battlefield and begin shaping it.

The technique was refined during the Wars of the Shattered Frontier, where Spellblades frequently fought against numerically superior forces. Rather than remaining locked in place against overwhelming odds, they learned to transform enemy attacks into opportunities for movement.

Masters of Arcane Reflex often appear impossible to pin down. Every attack seems to place them exactly where they wish to be, turning an enemy's aggression into a tool for their own positioning.

Many young Spellblades believe Arcane Reflex exists to avoid damage. Experienced masters know the truth: avoiding damage is merely the beginning. The real purpose is deciding where the battle happens.

> "A master does not avoid danger. They decide where danger is allowed to exist."
>
> — High Spellblade Arkanis Thorne, Warden of the Azure Depths

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Reflex reaches its pinnacle, transforming the Spellblade's defensive instincts into a seamless blend of awareness, protection, and opportunity. At this stage, reacting to danger is no longer a conscious decision—it is an extension of the Spellblade's very nature.

The moment an attack is launched, mana surges through the body, enhancing perception, reinforcing vulnerable areas, and preparing a path of escape before the threat has fully materialised. Every motion becomes precise, efficient, and deliberate.

What separates masters from apprentices is not merely their ability to survive an attack, but their ability to turn that survival into an advantage. A failed strike against a master Spellblade often becomes the first step toward an enemy's defeat.

At Rank 5, Arcane Reflex no longer exists solely to prevent harm. It allows the Spellblade to seize control of the battle's momentum and create openings where none previously existed.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **24 MP**.
- Gain **+4 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the triggering attack.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses your Reaction for the round.

#### Arcane Mitigation

If the triggering attack still hits:

- Reduce the damage taken by **1d6**.

#### Arcane Reposition

After the triggering attack resolves, whether it hits or misses:

- Instantly move up to **3 metres** to an unoccupied space you can see.
- This movement does **not** provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- You may move through enemy spaces but cannot end your movement inside one.
- You cannot move through solid walls, magical barriers, or impassable terrain.

#### Tactical Uses

Arcane Reposition may be used to:

- Break enemy engagement.
- Move behind cover.
- Reposition for your next attack.
- Escape hazardous terrain.
- Create distance from dangerous opponents.

### Lore

The oldest Spellblade records describe Rank 5 as the Stage of Anticipation. Practitioners no longer react to attacks in the traditional sense. Instead, they appear to move before danger fully manifests, as though they instinctively understand the shape of the battle moments before it unfolds.

Stories of legendary Spellblades often speak of warriors who seemed untouchable in combat. Opponents would launch strike after strike, only to find their target already gone, standing elsewhere with blade in hand and a counterattack prepared.

Scholars debate whether this level of Arcane Reflex is simply the result of extraordinary training or whether prolonged exposure to mana grants fleeting glimpses of future possibilities. Most Spellblades dismiss such theories, claiming that experience and discipline are sufficient explanations.

Whatever the truth, masters of Arcane Reflex are feared throughout Asteria. Every missed attack places them in a stronger position than before, turning an enemy's aggression into the very tool that leads to their downfall.

> "The novice reacts to danger. The master has already moved."
>
> — Grandmaster Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

# Arcane Rush

## Overview
The Spellblade learns to channel mana directly into movement, allowing them to cross short distances with unnatural speed. Rather than relying purely on physical strength, they infuse their body with arcane energy, creating a sudden burst of acceleration that carries them across the battlefield in the blink of an eye.

To an observer, the movement appears almost impossible to follow. One moment the Spellblade stands still, and the next they have surged forward, leaving only a faint trail of arcane energy in their wake.

At Rank 1, Arcane Rush is a simple but highly effective mobility technique. It allows the Spellblade to rapidly reposition, close the distance to an enemy, escape danger, or reach advantageous terrain without relying on conventional movement.

While the technique lacks the sophistication of higher ranks, it establishes the foundation upon which future mobility techniques will be built.

## Rank 1
### Description

The Spellblade learns to channel mana directly into movement, allowing them to cross short distances with unnatural speed. Rather than relying purely on physical strength, they infuse their body with arcane energy, creating a sudden burst of acceleration that carries them across the battlefield in the blink of an eye.

To an observer, the movement appears almost impossible to follow. One moment the Spellblade stands still, and the next they have surged forward, leaving only a faint trail of arcane energy in their wake.

At Rank 1, Arcane Rush is a simple but highly effective mobility technique. It allows the Spellblade to rapidly reposition, close the distance to an enemy, escape danger, or reach advantageous terrain without relying on conventional movement.

While the technique lacks the sophistication of higher ranks, it establishes the foundation upon which future mobility techniques will be built.

### Effects

- Spend **12 MP** to activate Arcane Rush.
- Instantly move up to **4 metres** to a visible location.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Arcane Rush may be used to:
  - Engage enemies.
  - Escape melee range.
  - Reposition around obstacles.
  - Reach advantageous terrain.
- Does not grant additional attacks.
- Does not increase movement speed outside of activation.

#### Movement Rules

- The destination must be within line of sight.
- You may move through enemy spaces during the rush.
- You cannot activate if you are engaged with an enemy.
- You cannot pass through solid walls, magical barriers, or completely blocked terrain.
- You must end the movement in a valid unoccupied space.

### Lore

Among Spellblades, Arcane Rush is often the first mobility technique taught after basic mana control. The ability demonstrates one of the core principles of the class: mana is not merely used for casting spells, but can be woven into every aspect of combat.

Veteran instructors frequently encourage students to master Arcane Rush before pursuing more advanced techniques. Proper positioning often determines the outcome of a battle long before the first strike is made.

Many duellists describe their first successful Arcane Rush as a transformative experience. For a brief moment, distance ceases to feel absolute, and the battlefield becomes something that can be navigated rather than endured.

Though simple in execution, countless Spellblades have survived impossible situations thanks to a well-timed Arcane Rush.

> "The quickest path is not always the shortest. Sometimes it is the one shaped by mana."
>
> — Blademaster Kaelis Vorn, Instructor of the Azure Path

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Spellblade's mastery of Arcane Rush grows, they learn to channel mana through their body more efficiently, allowing them to travel greater distances with each burst of arcane acceleration.

The technique becomes smoother and more controlled. Rather than forcing mana through the body in a sudden surge, the Spellblade learns to guide it naturally through their movements, extending both the range and reliability of the rush.

At Rank 2, Arcane Rush remains a mobility technique first and foremost. The Spellblade becomes capable of covering greater distances across the battlefield, allowing them to engage enemies, reposition, or escape danger with increased effectiveness.

Experienced Spellblades often describe this stage as the point where Arcane Rush begins to feel natural rather than forced, becoming a regular part of their combat style rather than a technique used only in emergencies.

### Effects

- Spend **15 MP** to activate Arcane Rush.
- Instantly move up to **6 metres** to a visible location.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Arcane Rush may be used to:
  - Engage enemies.
  - Escape melee range.
  - Reposition around obstacles.
  - Reach advantageous terrain.
- Does not grant additional attacks.
- Does not increase movement speed outside of activation.

#### Movement Rules

- The destination must be within line of sight.
- You may move through enemy spaces during the rush.
- You cannot activate if you are engaged with an enemy.
- You cannot pass through solid walls, magical barriers, or completely blocked terrain.
- You must end the movement in a valid unoccupied space.

### Lore

Among seasoned Spellblades, Rank 2 is often called the stage of refinement. The practitioner has moved beyond simply forcing mana into motion and begins to understand how arcane energy can enhance movement without overwhelming the body.

Many instructors encourage students to use Arcane Rush repeatedly during training exercises, not to increase speed, but to improve control. A rushed movement may reach its destination, but a controlled movement arrives exactly where it is needed.

Those who master this stage often find themselves viewing the battlefield differently. Obstacles become opportunities, distance becomes less intimidating, and positioning becomes a weapon in its own right.

> "The first rush teaches movement. The second teaches control."
>
> — Blademaster Kaelis Vorn, Instructor of the Azure Path

## Rank 3
### Description

The Spellblade's command over Arcane Rush reaches a level where distance begins to lose its meaning. Mana flows effortlessly through their body, carrying them across the battlefield with remarkable speed and precision.

What once felt like a burst of movement now feels like a natural extension of combat itself. The Spellblade no longer thinks about where they are standing, but where they need to be. Every engagement, retreat, and reposition becomes smoother as the technique evolves.

At Rank 3, Arcane Rush allows the Spellblade to traverse significant distances in an instant, making them increasingly difficult to pin down. Enemies who rely on controlling positioning often find themselves struggling to keep pace with a practitioner capable of appearing where they are least expected.

Many veterans consider this the stage where Arcane Rush transforms from a useful technique into a defining part of the Spellblade's combat identity.

### Effects

- Spend **18 MP** to activate Arcane Rush.
- Instantly move up to **8 metres** to a visible location.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Arcane Rush may be used to:
  - Engage distant enemies.
  - Escape melee range.
  - Reposition around obstacles.
  - Reach advantageous terrain.
  - Bypass enemy frontlines.
- Does not grant additional attacks.
- Does not provide offensive bonuses at this rank.

#### Movement Rules

- The destination must be within line of sight.
- You may move through enemy spaces during the rush.
- You may ignore difficult terrain during the movement.
- You cannot pass through solid walls, magical barriers, or completely blocked terrain.
- You must end the movement in a valid unoccupied space.

### Lore

Among experienced Spellblades, Rank 3 is often referred to as the Path Between Moments. Practitioners describe a strange sensation during movement, as though the distance travelled becomes shorter than it should be.

Some scholars argue that Arcane Rush does not truly increase speed, but instead allows the Spellblade to briefly slip through the spaces between mana currents that flow throughout the world. Whether this theory is true remains the subject of debate among arcane researchers.

What is certain is that those who master this stage become exceptionally difficult to contain. Opponents learn quickly that distance offers little protection against a Spellblade capable of crossing the battlefield in the blink of an eye.

Many legendary duels have been decided by a single perfectly timed Arcane Rush, carrying the practitioner to exactly the right place at exactly the right moment.

> "The battlefield belongs to the one who decides where the fight happens."
>
> — High Spellblade Arkanis Thorne, Warden of the Azure Depths

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade has mastered the fundamentals of Arcane Rush, allowing them to move across the battlefield with extraordinary speed and precision. What was once a method of repositioning has evolved into a technique that directly influences combat itself.

Mana now surges through the Spellblade's body with such efficiency that the momentum of the rush can be carried into their next action. The transition between movement and attack becomes seamless, creating openings that slower opponents struggle to react to.

At Rank 4, Arcane Rush no longer serves only as a mobility tool. The sudden acceleration and perfect positioning generated by the technique provide the Spellblade with a brief but valuable combat advantage immediately after arriving at their destination.

Veteran Spellblades often describe this stage as the point where movement and combat become one. Every rush becomes part of an attack, and every attack begins with movement.

### Effects

- Spend **21 MP** to activate Arcane Rush.
- Instantly move up to **12 metres** to a visible location.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Arcane Rush may be used to:
  - Engage distant enemies.
  - Escape melee range.
  - Reposition around obstacles.
  - Reach advantageous terrain.
  - Bypass enemy frontlines.
- Does not grant additional attacks.
- Does not provide offensive bonuses at this rank.

#### Arcane Momentum

After completing Arcane Rush:

- Your next attack before the end of your turn gains:
  - **+1 to Hit**

The bonus is consumed whether the attack hits or misses.

#### Movement Rules

- The destination must be within line of sight.
- You may move through enemy spaces during the rush.
- You may ignore difficult terrain during the movement.
- You cannot pass through solid walls, magical barriers, or completely blocked terrain.
- You must end the movement in a valid unoccupied space.

### Lore

Among the great Spellblade Orders, Rank 4 is often called the Stage of Momentum. At this point, practitioners no longer think of movement and combat as separate disciplines. Every reposition becomes an opportunity, and every opportunity becomes a potential strike.

Masters frequently train their students to attack immediately after an Arcane Rush, teaching them to exploit the brief confusion created by their sudden relocation. To outside observers, the technique can appear almost unfair, as the Spellblade seems to arrive already prepared to attack.

Historical accounts describe veteran Spellblades using Arcane Rush to cross entire battle lines before striking enemy commanders, mages, or siege crews. Their ability to appear where they were least expected often proved more dangerous than the attacks themselves.

Many duelists spend years attempting to predict where a Spellblade will move next. Most eventually learn the same lesson: by the time you see the rush, it is already too late.

> "The greatest advantage is not speed. It is arriving before your enemy understands that you have moved."
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aethon Vale, Master of the Sapphire Hall

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Rush reaches its ultimate form, transforming the Spellblade into a blur of motion and arcane energy. Distance becomes little more than a suggestion as the practitioner moves across the battlefield with breathtaking speed and precision.

The mana flowing through the Spellblade no longer merely enhances movement—it becomes movement. Every rush is executed with absolute confidence, carrying the Spellblade exactly where they need to be while creating the perfect opportunity for a decisive strike.

At Rank 5, Arcane Rush embodies one of the core principles of the Spellblade path: superior positioning creates superior opportunities. The Spellblade can appear where they are least expected, exploit weaknesses in enemy formations, and strike before opponents can properly react.

Among Spellblades, reaching this rank is considered a mark of mastery. Few possess the control, experience, and arcane endurance necessary to wield Arcane Rush at its highest level.

### Effects

- Spend **24 MP** to activate Arcane Rush.
- Instantly move up to **15 metres** to a visible location.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Arcane Rush may be used to:
  - Engage distant enemies.
  - Escape melee range.
  - Reposition around obstacles.
  - Reach advantageous terrain.
  - Bypass enemy frontlines.
  - Rapidly relocate across the battlefield.
- Does not grant additional attacks.
- Does not provide offensive bonuses at this rank.

#### Arcane Momentum

After completing Arcane Rush:

- Your next attack before the end of your turn gains:
  - **+2 to Hit**
  - **+1d4 Arcane Damage**

The bonus is consumed whether the attack hits or misses.

#### Movement Rules

- The destination must be within line of sight.
- You may move through enemy spaces during the rush.
- You may ignore difficult terrain during the movement.
- You cannot pass through solid walls, magical barriers, or completely blocked terrain.
- You must end the movement in a valid unoccupied space.

### Lore

The highest masters of Arcane Rush are often spoken of in legends and battlefield tales. Witnesses describe them as appearing and disappearing across the battlefield so quickly that it becomes difficult to determine where they truly are.

Military historians frequently record accounts of elite Spellblades crossing entire engagements to strike critical targets before defenders could react. Commanders learned to fear the sudden appearance of a Spellblade more than the approach of an army.

Among the Azure Orders, Rank 5 is known as the Horizon Step. The name comes from the belief that a true master sees no meaningful difference between where they stand and where they wish to be. Distance becomes an obstacle that can simply be ignored.

Those who achieve this rank have mastered more than movement. They have mastered opportunity itself, arriving precisely where fate demands and striking at the moment their enemies are least prepared.

> "The battlefield is not measured in distance. It is measured in opportunities. Arcane Rush simply ensures I reach them first."
>
> — Grandmaster Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well
